I just had the same issue. It's the first time it happened to me. I wasn't doing anything even close to be demanding. I literally had an empty scene. My File System had some empty scenes and some scripts, I had about 20 addons I wanted to test but only 3 out of 4 were active and the reset are all assets, but as I said not scene was active. The only thing of notice, is that I added a 3D GripMap node while an empty scene was running and godot was running for hours. 

What happened was that godot it's was running almost normally, and this error popped up, godot was still running, you could still run the project, add nodes, use the editor, etc..., but on the GirdMap, even though you could select the meshes, change modes (paint, remove, etc...), and even these changes are shown visibly in the editor, but the editor window itself didn't respond to mouse movements and clicks, so the mesh you select and editing tool are stock at vector.zero. 

Unfortunately, I tried replicating the issue in all sequences, but nothing happened. But that might be because I restarted the editor.

Hi!

I can reproduce this warning in nearly every run on my computer with a project that has no scripts or adons. It's attached as a zip, and I also made some measurements included below.

While I did encounter the issue myself; the reproduction, troubleshooting, and run script were made with an AI assistant. I have run the tests myself.

The tests exaggerate CPU starvation and back-to-back physics steps to make the warning reliable. Without the tests, I only saw it happen a few times (maybe 4/30 today, as I was writing the smoke test), but I didn't keep track. The smoke test that triggered it always ran with `--headless` and `--fixed-fps`. I haven't been aware of it happening in normal conditions.

**Where I first saw it**

My own C# project hit it a few times while running a smoke test. The test fails on any warning, which was happening at random on clean builds. 

The smoke test itself just compiled and ran the project for a few (fixed) seconds. The warning seemed to appear right after `dotnet build` and launching the project `--headless`, but I wasn't able to determine a specific timing. I had the editor open at the same time.

**Tested versions**
- 4.7.2.stable.mono.official [ed1daf0bf]. The reproduction project has no C#.
- 4.8.beta1.official [4d10419ca]. The other versions had similar results +/- 5 warnings p/run.
- 4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4]

**System information**
Godot v4.7.2.stable.mono - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 12 Oct 2026 06:58:10 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (nvidia; 615.78.08) - AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 30.49 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Unzip the project. `bodies.tscn` is a StaticBody3D floor with 64 RigidBody3D boxes falling onto it. It's using Jolt with `physics_ticks_per_second` at 480.
2. Run `./run_repro.sh`. It runs one instance at a time, 16 times, each as `taskset -c 0,1 godot --headless --path . --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after 300`, then counts the runs that printed the warning.

Only tested on Linux. Windows might need some adaptation.

**Results 4.7.2** (one instance at a time, 480 ticks per second)
| Setup | Runs with the warning |
|---|---|
| Pinned to 2 cores | 193 of 196 |
| Pinned to 1 core | 32 of 32 |
| Pinned to 4 cores | 20 of 32 |
| Pinned to 8 cores | 6 of 32 |
| No pinning (16 threads) | 5 of 48 |
| Pinned to 2 cores, `threading/worker_pool/max_threads=2` | 26 of 32 |
| Control: pinned to 2 cores, `empty.tscn` | 0 of 48 |
| Control: pinned to 2 cores, real time (no `--fixed-fps`) | 0 of 40 |

**Relevant commands** (same order)
./run_repro.sh res://bodies.tscn 1 196
PIN_CPUS=0 ./run_repro.sh res://bodies.tscn 1 32
PIN_CPUS=0-3 ./run_repro.sh res://bodies.tscn 1 32
PIN_CPUS=0-7 ./run_repro.sh res://bodies.tscn 1 32
PIN_CPUS= ./run_repro.sh res://bodies.tscn 1 48
printf '[threading]\nworker_pool/max_threads=2\n' > override.cfg && ./run_repro.sh res://bodies.tscn 1 32; rm -f override.cfg
./run_repro.sh res://empty.tscn 1 48
EXTRA_ARGS="--quit-after 300" ./run_repro.sh res://bodies.tscn 1 40

Last one is real-time, so it takes a bit to run.

Hope it helps!

[jolt-job-limit-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33605750/jolt-job-limit-mrp.zip)

That's great, thank you. I'm able to reproduce it now as well, using your MRP.

I haven't looked at what's happening exactly, but it seems that the actual scene itself is completely irrelevant. `--headless --fixed-fps` with even just a single body, coupled with pinning to 4 cores or less, seems to be what does it.

I'll take a closer look in the coming days/weeks, which should hopefully yield a fix for this, that can then go into 4.8.
